entities.summary: Marcus Claudius Fronto was a Roman senator and Consul, and a general in the Imperial Roman army during the reigns of emperors Antoninus Pius, Marcus Aurelius, and Lucius Verus. He served as Consul in 165 CE, a position he shared with the future emperor Lucius Verus. As a general, Fronto played a key role in the Roman army's campaigns against the Germanic tribes, including the Battle of Aeliana, where he distinguished himself with bravery and tactical prowess. His military service was marked by his ability to adapt to changing circumstances and lead his troops to victory in difficult terrain. Fronto's legacy extended beyond his military career, as he was also a respected orator and writer, whose works on rhetoric and philosophy were widely studied and admired in the ancient world. His writings on the nature of rhetoric and the importance of eloquence in public speaking were particularly influential, and his ideas on the subject can still be found in the writings of later Roman philosophers. Fronto's impact on Roman society was significant, as he helped to shape the country's military and political institutions, and his writings continue to be studied by historians and scholars today. Despite his importance, Fronto's life remains somewhat of a mystery, and much of what we know about him comes from the writings of other ancient historians, such as Cassius Dio and Ammianus Marcellinus. Nevertheless, his legacy as a Roman statesman, military leader, and scholar continues to be felt, and he remains an important figure in the history of ancient Rome.
